plugin.xor.title: XOR and the one-time pad
plugin.xor.preset.hello: "hello" in ASCII with a random-looking key
plugin.xor.preset.zero-key: All-zero key (the result equals the message)
plugin.xor.preset.key-equals-message: Key equals the message (the result is all zeros)
plugin.xor.preset.case-flip: Key 0x20 in every byte (flips ASCII upper/lower case)
plugin.xor.param.messageHint: 1 to 32 bytes as hex digits; spaces and colons are ignored.
plugin.xor.param.keyHint: Exactly as many bytes as the message; for a one-time pad, random and never reused.
plugin.xor.op.xorByte: XOR one byte of the message with the matching key byte
plugin.xor.op.decrypt: Decrypt – XOR the result with the same key
plugin.xor.step.initial: Message and key each have {{count}} bytes. XOR works on bits, so every byte is just 8 bits to combine: each key bit decides whether the matching message bit stays (0) or flips (1).
plugin.xor.step.xorByte: Byte {{index}}: {{message}} ⊕ {{key}} = {{result}}. Wherever the key has a 1 bit, the message bit flips.
plugin.xor.step.decrypt: XOR the result with the same key once more and the message comes back: (m ⊕ k) ⊕ k = m ⊕ (k ⊕ k) = m ⊕ 0 = m. XOR is its own inverse, so encrypting and decrypting are the same operation.
plugin.xor.error.invalidParams: Give the message and the key as hex text.
plugin.xor.error.messageLength: The message has {{length}} bytes; it needs 1 to 32.
plugin.xor.error.keyLength: The key has {{length}} bytes; it needs 1 to 32.
plugin.xor.error.lengthMismatch: The message has {{message}} bytes but the key has {{key}}; both must be equally long.
